noir.name: Noir
noir.summary: First person, past tense, a narrator who notices what he would rather not.
moves: Keep the sentences short and the paragraphs shorter; let a long one land only when it is doing work.
Report the room before the feeling — what is on the table, what the light is doing, who has not moved.
Let the narrator be wrong about himself and right about everyone else.
End a scene one beat before the reader is ready.
avoid: Period pastiche — fedoras, dames, gats — in place of an observed detail.
Explaining the narrator's mood in the narrator's voice.
A wisecrack where a silence would do more.

plain.name: Plain
plain.summary: An override: this entry replaces the built-in plain style outright.
moves: Put the actor before the action.
Say the number rather than the adjective: "eleven minutes", not "a long wait".
avoid: Any sentence that needs a second reading.
